profile.name: FOMC Member Speaks
profile.what: Remarks from a regional Fed president or governor.
profile.why_gold: Mostly background, but a known hawk turning dovish - or the reverse - is a genuine signal, and voting members matter more than non-voters.
profile.watch: Whether the speaker votes this year, and whether they are departing from their usual stance.
profile.gotchas: Several speakers a day is normal and almost always noise. Treat as background unless the tone genuinely shifts.

profile.name: Fed Chair Speaks
profile.what: Any scheduled appearance by the Fed Chair - testimony, conference remarks, or a moderated Q&A.
profile.why_gold: The Chair sets the policy narrative between meetings. A single sentence on the balance of risks can move the rate curve as much as a data release.
profile.watch: Whether the venue allows questions. Prepared remarks are usually safe; unscripted Q&A is where the surprises come from.
profile.gotchas: No forecast number exists, so nothing is priced in. The risk is pure tone, which makes it hard to hedge and easy to get run over by.

profile.name: Benchmark Payrolls Revision
profile.what: Annual re-benchmarking of the payroll survey against actual tax records, which can rewrite a whole year of job growth in one line.
profile.who: Bureau of Labor Statistics, preliminary in late summer, final in February
profile.why_gold: A large downward revision means the labour market was weaker than the Fed thought all along, which is dovish and gold-positive.
profile.watch: The size of the revision against the prior year's figure. Six figures is a serious number.
profile.gotchas: Once-a-year event that most calendars underrate. It can reprice the whole rate path in a single print.

profile.name: UoM Consumer Sentiment
profile.what: Michigan's household survey, released in preliminary and revised form at 15:00 UK.
profile.why_gold: The sentiment number is minor. The inflation-expectations component attached to it is not.
profile.watch: The 1-year and 5-10 year inflation expectations. The Fed watches the long-run figure closely, so a jump there is a genuine rate signal.
profile.gotchas: Small sample, frequently revised, and prone to reflecting petrol prices more than anything else.
